analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the 'Last updated' date, and a rewrite of the forced tool_choice paragraph near lines 2017-2040. The supplied head units (lines 417-1215) are unchanged surrounding documentation. Within them I examined the Nemotron Super admission and prefix-cache description, the GLM5Next boundary, and the calibration text. I found no new executable behavior, no new trust boundary, and no security control weakened.

The documented tool_choice change widens which builds the coordinator routes forced-tool requests to, via tool_constraint_models and ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.advertisesCapability. It adds Qwen3.5-9B, qwen3.5-35b-a3b, qwen3.6-35b-a3b-vl-mtp-mxfp8 and mimo-v2.6-flash-mopd, using prompt-forced, withheld, schema-validated post-validation. It also states that NativeToolStreamRouter drops framing whitespace (ASCII space, tab, CR, LF), that other Unicode whitespace is a tool_choice violation (422), and that whitespace alone counts as a missing call. This is a description of provider-side validation. The corresponding code was not supplied: ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.swift and NativeToolStreamRouter are outside the supplied units, so I cannot confirm the doc matches the implementation. Consumer-visible text is withheld and validated before exposure, which matches the existing fail-closed posture for T-008. Provider output manipulation (T-007) is unchanged in kind.

The prefix-cache text in the supplied range (SSD checkpoints encrypted under the provider's cache root, coordinator-authenticated cache scope, durable identity bound to pinned SHA-256 shards) is consistent with T-041 and does not alter it. The bank-versus-durable distinction and the 'no cache scope means off' behavior are unchanged in kind.

Remaining question for later passes: if the code PR that this doc describes expands forced-tool advertisement, check that the capability is advertised per exact build, that the mimo_v2 parser path is validated, and that the whitespace stripping cannot let hidden content through the router.
